editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 29 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.

editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Audit inherited session credentials before a child process inherits an agent inbox
dailyInsight.insight: Qwen Code's public main-branch change treats QWEN_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET and QWEN_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN as one capability. Operators building from this source or analogous runtimes should run a disposable nested-child check: a child that has not bound its own inbox must not retain either inherited value, while a child that binds a new inbox should receive only its own fresh pair.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The source adds a per-session token beside the inbox address, requires it before any incoming frame is read, carries a token on return receipts, and clears an inherited socket-and-token pair at the CLI entry point before any route can spawn a child. Focused tests cover malformed and wrong tokens, inherited-pair scrubbing, fresh-pair publication, and the fast paths that bypass the ordinary startup route.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A reachable local endpoint plus its valid credential can let a child or lifecycle script speak to an ancestor session. Auditing both values as one capability is a bounded way to catch an ownership leak before treating local cross-session messaging as a safe supervisory channel.

actions.audience: Qwen Code source-build or fork operators, and builders of comparable child-process agent runtimes
actions.label: Run a disposable inherited-capability check
actions.instruction: In a disposable environment, create one session inbox and launch a nested child that does not bind an inbox of its own. Verify that neither the inherited socket variable nor its token is present. Then launch a child that binds a new inbox and verify it receives a fresh pair that cannot authenticate to the ancestor. Do not use production credentials or live channels.

receipts.title: feat(ipc): authenticate cross-session inbox connections with per-session tokens (#10636)
receipts.supports: The public change describes the per-session credential, the ancestor-inbox inheritance risk, the entry-point scrub, and the focused regression coverage.

receipts.title: Inbox authentication and scripted injection
receipts.supports: The documentation identifies the first-line token gate and shows that a child hook needs the socket address and token together to inject a message.

receipts.title: CLI entry-point inherited-pair scrub
receipts.supports: The source removes the pair before managed-update, serve, MCP, or other CLI paths can start child processes.

receipts.title: Per-connection inbox authentication tests
receipts.supports: The focused tests cover required authentication, wrong-token refusal, and an inbox that remains usable after a refused connection.

confidence.basis: The fresh public commit, documentation, entry-point source, and focused tests agree on the capability-pair model and support a small reversible audit.

dailyInsight.limitation: These receipts establish intended Qwen Code main-branch behavior, not a tagged or deployed release, the security of a particular machine, or a field-wide conclusion about local IPC.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise or withdraw this call if public source or a regression demonstrates that a child which has not bound its own inbox retains the ancestor socket-and-token pair after CLI entry, or can inject into the ancestor with such a pair.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for a tagged release, package metadata that includes this commit, and cross-platform regression coverage for the named-pipe transport the design is intended to support.
